questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Experiences outside university life, another culture and nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been a good time, the university is nice but I felt very "stuck" in Auckland. For me, buying a van to go outside the city was crucial and on a Master's level degree you are very much left on your own in many ways. There is not really any activities arranged from the university so you have to make a real effort to make connections.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was a little confusing and to call anyone is impossible so you have to be good at mailing back and forth.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a friend to pick me up from the airport and showed up to my classes. I had already signed up for my subjects beforehand but it seems like you can still do that on arrival. I maybe did not have to have stressed so much about it in Denmark.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Again, I think it is very hard not being able to call the international office with any questions but being forced to write mails. I find that very criticisable.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No. I was offered to live with a family friend.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to be away from campus too.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not look into that because of my situation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very hard to figure out the course catalouge but once a friend helped me with it it became somewhat easier. But I felt like it was a lottery and that I did not really get the subjects that I wanted but that was also okay in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just followed the guidelines given

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student hub where other students are ready to help. But I registred before leaving Denmark.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Of the classes I could choose from in the end I got every one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that exchange is also other experiences that classes and be flexible in your choices. It is hard to know beforehand how the classes are anyway and there is a short period of time after the clesses start that you can change if needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very happy with my one online class, the overall recordings of classes in general and the professional yet kind professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think they were all master level courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was really good. Professors were approachable and the environment friendly. But it varied from class to class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Nutrition interventions is public health 

People participation and development 

Public Health (online)

Project planning for lifestyle change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: People participation and development! JC is the best professor and the class I enjoyed to most and made most friends.

questions.answer: A specialist doctor that I had to go to to get some medication. 2500 DKK

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Phone company is more expensive and food too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They gym is really nice and big, also sport clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Quite a lot if you started to look into it. But I did not really engage much in those.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for the gym and go to Grafton Campus activities

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to surrounding areas of Auckland. Piha e.g.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Just a few small other things to know.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people in your classes and ask them if they want to do something together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very very friendly, open and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go out of Auckland to explore because the city life is not so charming. 
Seek help if needed.
Nyd oplevelsen med alt hvad det indebærer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be more independent and learn about another country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The classes were harder than expected and also to deal with all the social on top of that was mentally draining

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
